newsitem.title: UK: LME copper ends day barely changed, aimless.
newsitem.headline: LME copper ends day barely changed, aimless.

text.p: LME copper finished Monday virtually unchanged after spinning its wheels most of the day in lacklustre activity.
Most other metals followed copper's lead, holding to narrow price bands and showing little direction.
Three months copper ended the afternoon kerb 50 cents firmer at $2,288.50 per tonne after trading between $2,276 and $2,293.
For the past two weeks copper has oscillated in a range fenced by $2,245 on the downside and $2,309 on the upside.

Prices surged to the psychological $2,300 level on Friday when some workers at Chile's huge Escondida mine went on strike, but when the mini-rally failed, the market lost the little life it had shown.

Players are reluctant to sell the market as long as it remains unclear whether any effect would be felt from the strike at Escondida, in which 353 workers representing 17 percent of the workforce are off the job.
The company said on Friday the stoppage would not reduce output and there was no confirmation of an analyst's report on Monday that ore extraction had already been affected.
Broker GNI said stockpiles were being used in the mill and concentrator at Escondida -- the world's largest copper mine -- and only one week's supply remained.
Company officials in Chile were not immediately available to comment.
"I still think copper is showing a bias to the upside. I'm looking for it to try at $2,300 again in the short-term," said analyst Martin Squires of broker Rudolf Wolff.
The premium of cash over May remained firm at $10/$14 after that spread moved into backwardation on Friday and the cash/threes rate was wider at a $62/$64 backwardation from $45/$50 on Friday.
Lead drifted back above above the day's weakest price of $624, a fresh low since October 1995. It ended with a $3 loss at $628.
The break lower has damaged the charts and the market could easily sink to test $600 in the near-term, traders and analysts said.
Only if the market regained $645/50 would the bearish scenario have to be called off, they added.

"Lead looks pretty sick...you're looking at $615 and $600, but there won't be any aggressive selling," Squires said, adding that another build in stocks was expected on Tuesday after a rise of 3,275 tonnes on Monday.
Aluminium tagged along with copper, edging a touch higher on the kerb, but ending only $1 firmer at $1,555.
Nickel showed a minor burst of strength in the afternoon, lifting off a morning low of $7,280 to touch $7,390, but failed to break above that level which was also the high on Friday.
Last business on the kerb was at $7,380, up $35.
Tin lost $5 to $5,710 while zinc gained $1 to $1,248.
Alloy was last indicated barely changed at $1,447/40.
--Eric Onstad, London Newsroom ++44 171 542-8065
